Subject: Sandbox preflight + SDK architect map for Clearwell PoC

Hi Sam / Anita —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap plus a pragmatic preflight so your engineering team can spin up a local sandbox and validate the integration surface before the formal PoC starts. I kept this intentionally action-oriented so you can forward to your infra/dev teams.

High-level summary
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference flow for triage summarization and a basic reranker step in Clearwell's ingestion pipeline (no PHI left in Redwood during sandbox).
- Scope for preflight: local SDK install (Python + TS example), OAuth token auth flow (short-lived tokens + rotation sample), routing to hosted dev model, basic structured output for tool-calling (extraction -> reranker), and a smoke test for embeddings + rerank.

Immediate asks (who/when)
1) Engineering point: Can your infra lead provision a machine with Docker + npm + Python3.10 by Wed 5/19? (Sam)
2) Sandbox owner: Please confirm an internal email we can use to mint a developer token for the sandbox (expires in 7 days). We will provide a scoped token and rotation example. (Anita)
3) UX/PO: Provide 2 representative prompts for summarization and 20 sample doc snippets for the reranker seed dataset (sample size can be smaller if needed).

Deliverables attached and links
- redwood_sdk_sandbox_steps.pdf (attached): step-by-step local run, environment variables, Docker snippets.
- auth-token-rotation-example.txt (attached): a tiny script showing short-lived token exchange.
- sample-routing-config.yaml (attached): example of route rules to send low-priority traffic to a cheaper quantized model in the sandbox.
- Repo with examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/clearwell-samples
- HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/4832

Technical notes for your SRE (short)
- Local run will use our hosted dev models; no model artifacts need to be pulled.
- Prefix caching can be disabled for the first run (see step 5 in PDF) to simplify validation; we'll re-enable it when you validate latency profiles.
- Embeddings: we recommend batch size 64 for local tests unless you have <4GB GPU memory.

Next call
- Suggest a 30-min tech preflight on Thu 5/20 at 09:00 PT to walk through the sample run if your team wants a live ramp.

Thanks — I copied Marissa, Karthik and Priyom for any sales/engineering follow-ups.

—

Sam —

Addressing the two security/engineering points you raised:

1) Audit logs / telemetry: For the sandbox we can provide a minimal request log that includes: timestamp, route, request_id (obfuscated), model_key_used, and response latency. We will not log request text in the shared telemetry bundle; if you want request-level logs we can run a separate, customer-managed log collector in your VPC during Private mode.

2) Safe local tool-calling: For the preflight we recommend a "dry-run" tool-calling mode documented in the attached PDF (see section 4):
   - The SDK supports structured-output only, without executing any webhook. The sample app returns the structured payload (i.e., function name + args) and writes it to a local file for inspection instead of invoking external endpoints.
   - If you want to test a real webhook, we suggest running it against a local mock (ngrok or a simple Docker mock) that you control — the SDK can be configured to use the mock's URL.

3) Reranker data masking: Masking a small number of fields will not materially change reranker effectiveness if you preserve semantic cues. For edge cases we can ship a small synthetic augmentation script to restore context signals (we include a sample in the repo).

4) Embeddings memory: If you plan to run embedding batching locally without GPU, set batch_size to 8-16 depending on RAM. The sample app switches automatically if CUDA is available.

I also pushed a tiny change to the sample repo that adds a --dry-run flag to the tool-caller example so you can validate structured output without side effects.

—Karthik
